description:
Fact-check a claim about a CVE against the corpus — catch hallucinations
before they ship. Verifies: does the CVE exist; does it affect the claimed
product at the claimed version; is the severity right; is it actually
KEV-exploited. Returns per-assertion verdicts (supported / refuted /
unverifiable) with cited evidence.

Use it to check what another agent (or a draft report) asserted, e.g.
"Spring4Shell (CVE-2022-22965) is critical, actively exploited, and affects Spring 5.3.18" →
verify_cve_claim("CVE-2022-22965", product="spring framework", version="5.3.18",
                 severity="critical", exploited=True)   (the version claim is refuted: fixed in 5.3.18).
A distro build as product/version ("OpenSSH_9.2p1 Debian-2+deb12u3", or version "1:9.2p1-2+deb12u3")
adds a second assertion with the distro's own verdict for that build. A CNA-rejected id comes back
exists=true with rejected=true: treat any claim citing it as unsupported.

Args:
    cve_id: the CVE/GHSA/PYSEC id being claimed about.
    product / version: optional — checks the affected-version claim in range.
    severity: optional — a CVSS number ("9.8") or label ("critical"/"high"/…).
    exploited: optional bool — the "actively exploited / in KEV" claim.
    claim: optional free text — returns evidence (summary, CWE) for you to judge.
name: verify_cve_claim
title: Fact-check a CVE claim
